relationships.subject: Stomatin
relationships.evidence_quote: STOM dramatically inhibits ASIC3 currents by nearly 200-fold [16,17].

relationships.subject: CIPP
relationships.evidence_quote: Whole-cell current measurements of cells co-expressing ASIC3 and CIPP resulted in an alkaline shift in the pH dependence of activation and an additional ~5-fold increase in current magnitude at saturating pH [36].

relationships.subject: PSD-95
relationships.evidence_quote: Binding of the two proteins did not alter ASIC gating, but led to a ~5-fold decrease in ASIC3 current due to a decrease in ASIC3 protein on the plasma membrane and also led to clustering of the channel [59].

relationships.subject: ASIC1a
relationships.evidence_quote: Wang et al. suggested that the acidification of the extracellular solution induced a physical association between ASIC1a and RIPK1 which led to the phosphorylation of RIPK1 and the triggering of necroptosis [49].

key_findings: Review of ASIC regulation by binding partners (stomatin, CIPP, PSD-95, NHERF, RIPK1 and others).
Stomatin strongly inhibits ASIC3 in an isoform-dependent manner via C-terminus and TM1 interactions.
